text.p: TROON, Scotland, July 16 - Fact file on Eldrick "Tiger" Woods, favourite for the British Open:
In 1978, aged two, appeared on U.S. television putting with Bob Hope.
Shot 48 for nine holes at the Navy Golf Club, California, when only three.
Won the Optimist International junior world title six times between the ages of eight and 15.
Became youngest player to win U.S. junior amateur championship at age of 15. Won it again the following year, the only golfer to win it twice, and took the title a third time in 1993.
Made his first appearance on the U.S. professional Tour when still only 16 in the Los Angeles Open. Scored rounds of 72 and 75 and missed the cut.
Became youngest U.S. amateur champion in 1994 aged 18 and retained title in each of the next two years, the only player to win championship in three successive years.
Played in U.S. Masters for first time aged 19 in 1995 and tied for 41st place. First appearance in British Open the same year and tied 67th.
Turned professional in August 1996 and in eight U.S. Tour events that year won two and also became the first player since Curtis Strange to record five consecutive top-five finishes.
Made the fastest rise from amateur status to top 100 in world ranking in six weeks, top 50 (eight weeks) and top 10 (33 weeks).

In 1997 set several records in winning U.S. Masters, lowest ever score of 18-under-par 270, widest winning margin of 12 strokes and at age of 21 years and three months 14 days, the youngest Masters champion.

Woods became youngest world number one on June 15, 1997 aged 21 years and 24 weeks and in only his 42nd week as a professional. The previous youngest was Bernhard Langer who was 29 years and 31 weeks when he headed the rankings in 1986.
In his first 10 months as a professional, Woods has seven tournament wins.
